title: Casual Minimum Wage Australia: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert casual minimum wage Australia to annual pay. Understand the 38-hour week, casual loading, tax, and super. State differences in ordinary-time earnings explained
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the casual minimum wage in Australia is $33.05 per hour including 25% loading, giving an annual gross of about $65,290 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual minimum wage in Australia for 2026–27?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. With the 25% casual loading, the casual minimum wage becomes $33.05 per hour. This applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many awards set higher rates, so check your specific award.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my casual hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. If you receive casual loading, ensure you use the rate that includes the 25% loading (do not add it again). This gives an approximate annual gross figure.

faqs.q: Do average earnings differ between states for casual workers?
faqs.a: Yes, average ordinary-time earnings vary by state due to industry mix and local economic conditions. The national full-time adult ordinary time average is $2,083.70 per week (ABS, May 2026), but state figures can be higher or lower. The National Minimum Wage and casual loading are the same nationwide, but award rates may include location-based allowances.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly to Annual

If you’re paid by the hour, converting your rate to an annual figure helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This article assumes a 38-hour week unless stated otherwise, as that is the full-time ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards.

For casual workers, the calculation includes the 25% casual loading paid on top of the base rate. The **casual minimum wage australia** is a key reference point for many workers, but remember that award rates and enterprise agreements often set higher minimums.

## The National Minimum Wage and Casual Loading

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the base rate is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, bringing the casual minimum wage to **$33.05 per hour**. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

It’s important to distinguish between:
- **National Minimum Wage**: the legal floor for award-free employees.
- **Award rates**: higher minimums set by industry or occupation awards.
- **Casual loading**: paid on top of the base rate, not included in the base.

When using a calculator, always enter your **base hourly rate** (before loading) and tick the casual loading box if applicable. Do not type a rate that already includes the 25% loading.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

While the National Minimum Wage is uniform across Australia, average ordinary-time earnings differ by state. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), full-time adult ordinary time earnings nationally averaged **$2,083.70 per week** in May 2026. However, this is an **average** across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. For example, workers in New South Wales and Victoria tend to earn above the national average, while those in Tasmania and South Australia often earn below. These differences reflect industry composition, cost of living, and local labour markets.

If you’re comparing a salary offer or your current pay, check the ABS data for your state and industry. Our [reference tables](/data) provide national benchmarks, but for a personalised estimate, use the [timesheet](/) on our home page.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Your annual gross pay is only part of the picture. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies a progressive tax scale for 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Most residents also pay a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 thresholds as 2026–27 reductions were not confirmed). 

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a casual worker on the minimum wage, super would be approximately $7,835 per year (12% of $65,290).

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide to estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) is the simplest way to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and tick the casual loading box if you receive it. The calculator applies the formula and shows gross annual pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: the result is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

For more details on casual loading, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page. If you want to compare your pay to industry averages, check the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) section.

## Final Thoughts

Knowing your annual equivalent helps you make informed decisions about jobs and finances. The **casual minimum wage australia** is a starting point, but your actual pay may be higher under an award or agreement. Always verify your entitlements with the Fair Work Ombudsman or your employer. Our calculator and guides are here to help you understand the numbers.
